title: JavaScript Metaprogramming Core Check
description: Check your understanding of object introspection, property descriptors, getters and setters, symbols, custom iterables, Reflect, proxies, and practical metaprogramming cautions.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What does JavaScript metaprogramming usually involve?

options.text: Inspecting or customizing how objects, functions, or language operations behave
Removing all objects from a program
Turning every function into a Promise

questions.explanation: Metaprogramming means code works with the structure or behavior of other code and objects.

questions.prompt: Which method returns a descriptor for an object's own property?
questions.explanation: `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor()` returns descriptor details such as `value`, `writable`, `enumerable`, and `configurable`.

questions.prompt: What does the `enumerable` descriptor field control?

options.text: Whether common enumeration tools like `Object.keys()` include the property
Whether the property can only contain numbers
Whether the property belongs to a class

questions.explanation: `enumerable` controls whether the property appears in common enumeration. It does not make data private.

questions.prompt: What is surprising about properties created with `Object.defineProperty()` when descriptor fields are omitted?

options.text: Boolean fields like `writable`, `enumerable`, and `configurable` default to `false`
They always become deeply frozen arrays

questions.explanation: Unlike assignment-created properties, `Object.defineProperty()` defaults omitted boolean descriptor fields to `false`.

questions.prompt: Which descriptor shape represents an accessor property?

options.text: A descriptor with only `writable` and no function

questions.explanation: Accessor descriptors use `get` and/or `set`; data descriptors use `value` and `writable`.

options.text: It is `false` because each `Symbol()` call creates a unique symbol
It is `true` because the descriptions match
It throws because symbols cannot have descriptions
It is `true` only in strict mode

questions.explanation: A symbol description is a debugging label, not its identity.

questions.prompt: Which method returns own symbol keys from an object?
questions.explanation: `Object.getOwnPropertySymbols()` returns own symbol property keys. `Object.keys()` returns enumerable string keys.

options.text: How an object is iterated by `for...of`, spread, and `Array.from()`

questions.explanation: `Symbol.iterator` defines the iterable protocol for an object.

questions.prompt: What should an iterator's `next()` method return?
questions.explanation: The iterator protocol expects `next()` to return `{ value, done }` objects.

questions.prompt: Why is `Reflect` often used inside proxy traps?

options.text: It delegates to the default operation while keeping trap code explicit
It converts every object to JSON

questions.explanation: `Reflect` methods are useful in traps because they perform the normal operation after custom behavior is added.

questions.prompt: Which proxy trap intercepts property reads?
questions.explanation: The `get` trap runs when code reads a property through the proxy.

questions.prompt: Which proxy trap intercepts calling a function proxy?
questions.explanation: The `apply` trap runs when a proxied function is called. `construct` runs for `new`.
